# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## PR Description

Closes #952
## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).
- `js/smAgent.js` (b): the #633/gh-750 self-clear rungs both sit behind the substantive-commit/park-time probes — during the incident window's CLI outage the null-guard fail-closed HOLD every tick, making a machine park permanent. New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). Rung is machine-scoped and sha-keyed — the fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 guest contracts (machine pushes never speak for a guest) are untouched, verified by the untouched pinned tests.

```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## PR Description

Closes #952
## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

Now check a few things in smAgent.js:

1. `clearStalePark952` — placed after `parkedHeadSha` at line ~6229, but it's called from `processRule` at line ~1945. Is `clearStalePark952` a function declaration (hoisted)? Yes — `function clearStalePark952(...)` so hoisting is fine within module scope.

2. In the gh-952 branch: `parkedHeadVf` — could be `null`; the check `parkedHeadVf &&` handles that. Good.

3. `probeHeadVerdictVf()` — memoized. In the outage case, `latestDispatchedVerdict` fails → null → !== 'failure' → clears. OK, matches #633 fail-open semantics.

4. `dropOpenPrsCache(repoInfo)` — check this function exists and is used in other unpark paths. In the #633 path and gh-750 path, is there a cache drop? The test expects capturedIoCacheDrops kind 'openPrs'. Check other clear paths — the sibling paths (headChangedNoVerdictVf) don't seem to drop cache in what I see... but gh-952 claims "same-tick slot yield". Let me check whether other unpark paths drop the cache. If they don't, is gh-952's drop consistent? Actually the comment says "Same side effects as every other park clear ... plus the same-tick slot yield: the open-PR cache drop". So it claims every other park clear also drops cache — but I don't see dropOpenPrsCache in the other paths in the excerpt above. Hmm, maybe dropOpenPrsCache is called elsewhere after unparkedThisPass. Let me grep.

5. The `isMachineParkPush` extraction — verify the old behavior identical.

6. mergeBot: check `deadHeadPassed` usage downstream in the FIFO loop.

Key observation in the mergeBot FIFO loop: `var approved = ...` and the `!validating || agent:review` branch. Note line 456: `deadHeadPassed = false;` — when an ARMED open PR is encountered, deadHeadPassed is reset to false. So the gh-952 release sets `deadHeadPassed = true` before the loop. But wait — there's a subtle interplay: the gh-952 release block sets `deadHeadPassed = true` when no OPEN armed holder exists. Inside the loop, any armed PR resets it to false (line 456). But armedHolderOpen already ensured no armed+approved PR exists. However, a dev-lane armed PR (ai_validating without pr_approved) — at line 425, `validating` true → goes to the armed branch → line 456 `deadHeadPassed = false`? Wait no: for a dev-lane arm, `validating` is true and `agent:review` not in labels → skips the first branch, hits line ~452-456: "An armed PR is a LIVE head by default" → deadHeadPassed = false. So a dev-lane armed PR (which per the PR description does NOT hold the merge window) would reset deadHeadPassed, killing the gh-952 release advance for the validated candidate behind it. Hmm — but does that matter? The release matters when a validated candidate should advance. If a dev-lane arm exists ahead in FIFO order... but FIFO sort is by number, and the loop processes in order. If a dev-lane armed PR with a lower number comes first, deadHeadPassed resets to false and the validated candidate behind can't advance. Is that a bug? Dev-lane arms don't hold the merge window (mutexAmong parity per the code comment and the test 'a dev-lane arm does not hold the merge-window slot'). The gh-952 release code computed armedHolderOpen with the same mutex parity (requires both ai_validating AND pr_approved). So the release deliberately fires when only dev-lane arms exist. But the loop's `deadHeadPassed = false` at the armed PR branch (line 456) would then consume the release silently. However — is that a practical problem? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 956
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/956
- **Title**: gh-952 merge-bot slot never re-arms after externally-merged PR (fa #1563 queued 3h with green checks)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-952` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +707
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T09:04:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T10:47:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #952
## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).
- `js/smAgent.js` (b): the #633/gh-750 self-clear rungs both sit behind the substantive-commit/park-time probes — during the incident window's CLI outage the null-guard fail-closed HOLD every tick, making a machine park permanent. New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). Rung is machine-scoped and sha-keyed — the fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 guest contracts (machine pushes never speak for a guest) are untouched, verified by the untouched pinned tests.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
# 2981 passed, 0 failed (suites: run_machineSmAgent 37, run_mergeBot 40,
# run_smAgent 552 — each carries a gh-952 suite)
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph machineSmAgent
    R[activeMachineRuns] --> G{linked PR MERGED?}
    G -->|orphan| DROP[drop from slot count + release log]
    G -->|live / unknown| HOLD[counts toward cap]
  end
  subgraph mergeBot
    O[open PRs] -->|no armed holder| M[probe merged list 24h]
    M -->|armed + fresh| V[vacate FIFO head]
  end
  subgraph smAgent park ladder
    P[park probes failed] -->|machine PR + park-comment sha differs + no fresh red| C[clear label + cache drop]
    P -->|guest / sha equal / fresh red| KEEP[keep park fail-closed]
  end
```

</details>

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 07:00–08:10Z, IstiN/flutter_agent_harness:

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.

New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

1. `clearStalePark952` — placed after `parkedHeadSha` at line ~6229, but it's called from `processRule` at line ~1945. Is `clearStalePark952` a function declaration (hoisted)? Yes — `function clearStalePark952(...)` so hoisting is fine within module scope.

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T10:47:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #952
## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).
- `js/smAgent.js` (b): the #633/gh-750 self-clear rungs both sit behind the substantive-commit/park-time probes — during the incident window's CLI outage the null-guard fail-closed HOLD every tick, making a machine park permanent. New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). Rung is machine-scoped and sha-keyed — the fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 guest contracts (machine pushes never speak for a guest) are untouched, verified by the untouched pinned tests.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
# 2981 passed, 0 failed (suites: run_machineSmAgent 37, run_mergeBot 40,
# run_smAgent 552 — each carries a gh-952 suite)
```

flowchart TD

    G -->|orphan| DROP[drop from slot count + release log]
    G -->|live / unknown| HOLD[counts toward cap]
  end
  subgraph mergeBot
    O[open PRs] -->|no armed holder| M[probe merged list 24h]
    M -->|armed + fresh| V[vacate FIFO head]
  end
  subgraph smAgent park ladder
    P[park probes failed] -->|machine PR + park-comment sha differs + no fresh red| C[clear label + cache drop]
    P -->|guest / sha equal / fresh red| KEEP[keep park fail-closed]
  end
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).
